paragraphs: Here's what I see in this chapter, friend. Nobody in Israel gets to decide for himself whether he's clean. The LORD gives the priest a careful way to look, and the priest looks, waits, and looks again (Leviticus 13:3-6). No guessing, no rushing, no rumors from the neighbors. I think that's a lot of patience, and it tells me God doesn't want anybody called unclean by accident.

Now look at the hard part. The person with the disease had to cry out, "Unclean, unclean!" and live alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:45-46). I think this one hurts, and I won't rush past it. Sin and its damage are serious, and this chapter shows that being separated from God's people is a heavy thing. But notice the other side too. The priest could say "clean" just as easily as "unclean," and the whole chapter keeps leaving that door open (Leviticus 13:6, 13:17, 13:34).

So what do I take from this, baker? God cares about what's really going on, not just what it looks like on the surface. Even the clothes got checked, and the LORD gave a way to get them clean again (Leviticus 13:58). I spent years forgotten in a drawer, so I know how much it matters that somebody looks closely and doesn't write you off. The teaching on clean and unclean isn't finished yet, so keep your oven warm and come back for more.
